subject: Why the same code is working only once

messages.author: 862dcfdada8cc0b2
messages.subject: Why the same code is working only once
parts:
I have this code in shiny server. The first chunk of code works well while the second one does not work. i am highly surprised with this . The code is same but only one is working.. don't know Y?? Am i missing something here.??


fulldata <- reactive({
    withProgress(  message = 'Generating Final Summary . . .',value= 0.01,{
      finaldata1 <- data()
      finaldata1 <- ldply(finaldata1, data.frame)[,-1]  ## To merge all the bins for final data
      finaldata1 <- finaldata1[,-2]  ## Removing second column
      finaldata1[is.na(finaldata1)] <- 0
      print(finaldata1)
    })
})


 summary1 <- reactive({
    finaldata2 <- fulldata()
    finaldata2 <- finaldata2[, c(1,2,seq(5,ncol(finaldata2),3))]
    print(finaldata2)
  })
 
  summary2 <- reactive({  ## this block is not running
    finaldata3 <- fulldata()
    finaldata3 <- finaldata3[, c(1,2,seq(4,ncol(finaldata3),3))]
    print(finaldata3)
  })

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Why the same code is working only once
parts:
summary1 and summary2 are reactive expressions, and as such, neither can cause themselves to run; they need to actually be used by an output (or an observer), either directly or through another reactive expression.

In other words, reactive expressions are lazily loaded. For this reason, you rarely want to call print() from inside of them--that's an example of a side effect and reactive expressions should not be used for side effects, except maybe while you're debugging whether/why it is/isn't executing.

If you want summary2 to be called, either change reactive() to observe(), or create another observer and call summary() from it:
observe({
  summary2()
})

See these articles for more info:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/execution-scheduling.html
